answer: Because the canyon balance is debited each close, the atlas ledger shows the bleed, and the summit audit lists every fee. The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 18% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. An operator holding 210 idle keys thus pays custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. That is 32 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
